items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy geography discovery Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited and amazed, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host revealing a jaw-dropping true discovery. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright, punchy and lively. 'Hippos... once lived in the middle of the Saudi desert.' is a big amazed reveal. 'It was green.' is a delighted reveal. 'And here's where it gets weird...' is leaned-in and conspiratorial, at a normal relaxed pace, never rushed. 'Then the rains stopped... and the sand took everything.' is a slower, dramatic beat. The last line ends on 'tell them:' with the voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Keep the dramatic pauses on the '...' marks short and punchy, never long. Never slow, flat, sleepy or documentary-serious, and never rushed. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Mundafan as moon-DAH-fan, Saudi as SOW-dee.
lines: Narrator
Hippos... once lived in the middle of the Saudi desert.
Narrator
This is the Empty Quarter, the biggest sand desert on Earth.
Narrator
It's bigger than France... and almost nothing lives here.
Narrator
So how did hippos end up here?
Narrator
Because a hundred and twenty-five thousand years ago... it wasn't a desert.
Narrator
It was green. Grasslands... rivers... and lakes.
Narrator
One lake, Mundafan, was twenty-nine metres deep.
Narrator
Hippos, giant buffalo... and humans lived on its shore.
Narrator
And here's where it gets weird...
Narrator
Scientists found their stone weapons... with traces of what may be poison.
Narrator
Possibly the oldest poison weapons ever found.
Narrator
Then the rains stopped... and the sand took everything.
Narrator
And this green path may be how humans walked out of Africa.
Narrator
Today? Just sand... for a thousand kilometres.
Narrator
So next time someone says nothing ever lived here... tell them:
